objective.statement: Manage the Factory Droid Remote Control daemon lifecycle through the dotfiles Home Manager profile instead of an ad hoc foreground process.
objective.measure: The cc-se-sto-devbox-01 Home Manager profile owns one enabled droid-remote-control user service, the service runs the managed Droid wrapper with daemon --remote-control, and live readback shows the service active with the registered computer reachable through the relay.

need.statement: Factory Remote Control on this devbox needs a persistent, managed daemon lifecycle.
stakeholders: Factory Remote Control clients and the operator on cc-se-sto-devbox-01
need.baseline: Droid 0.250.0 is registered as cc-se-sto-devbox-01, but .dotfiles has no Droid daemon lifecycle module or systemd user unit; Remote Control currently depends on a foreground process started outside the managed profile.
need.consequence_of_no_action: Remote Control disappears when the ad hoc process or host session ends, and no managed owner restores it.
alternatives_considered: Keep the ad hoc foreground process
Use a native Droid daemon lifecycle manager
Manage a systemd user service from the dotfiles Home Manager profile

purpose: Manage the Factory Droid Remote Control daemon lifecycle through the dotfiles Home Manager profile instead of an ad hoc foreground process.
consumer: Factory Remote Control clients and the operator on cc-se-sto-devbox-01
contract: On the cc-se-sto-devbox-01 Home Manager profile, one enabled droid-remote-control systemd user service shall run the managed ~/.local/bin/droid wrapper with daemon --remote-control, start only when the local computer registration exists, restart on failure, and receive the MiniMax primary, MiniMax backup, Kimi, and Ollama API-key environment variables from a mode-0600 provider-env file rendered from SOPS secrets before the daemon starts; the live Factory custom-model catalog shall expose the MiniMax backup key as a distinct BYOK route while the primary routes continue to use MINIMAX_API_KEY, and the service must be observable as active with the expected relay process and provider environment.
failure_boundary: The service remains user-scoped and fails closed when this machine is not registered. Provider keys exist only in mode-0600 runtime env files sourced from existing SOPS secrets; tracked files and Nix-store artifacts contain no key values. A failed Droid process is retried only by its own systemd unit, unrelated Codex daemon ownership is unchanged, and no Factory account or credential state is modified.

evidence.description: The dotfiles contract test proves the module import, managed wrapper command, registration condition, default-target enablement, ordered SOPS-backed primary and MiniMax-backup provider-env rendering, environment injection, and failure-restart policy.

Live readback proves droid-remote-control.service is active, the service process contains the MiniMax primary, MiniMax backup, Kimi, and Ollama API-key variables without exposing their values, the Factory custom-model catalog contains one distinct MiniMax backup route, droid computer list identifies cc-se-sto-devbox-01 as this machine, and a controlled native-daemon termination causes systemd to restart the unit.

falsifier.claim: The dotfiles profile owns a persistent Droid Remote Control daemon with the declared lifecycle contract.

executable_check.description: Any missing lifecycle declaration or failure of the focused contract test falsifies the source contract; any inactive service or missing relay readback falsifies the runtime claim.
executable_check.command: node --test --test-name-pattern="Droid Remote Control owns the daemon lifecycle" scripts/test-nix-tooling.mjs

non_goals: Automatically register or remove computers in the Factory account
Change Factory models, credentials, settings, or authentication
Change the Codex native daemon ownership
Modify unrelated dirty changes in the canonical dotfiles primary
invariants: The Codex managed daemon remains the sole owner of Codex app-server lifecycle
Droid computer registration remains local machine state and is not managed by dotfiles
Provider API-key values remain outside tracked files and Nix-store artifacts
The MiniMax primary and backup credentials remain distinct and independently selectable
At most one Home Manager systemd user service owns Droid Remote Control on this host
Unrelated canonical primary edits remain untouched

assumptions.statement: Droid daemon --remote-control stays in the foreground under a systemd user service and exits non-zero when no local registration exists.
assumptions.falsifier: A direct droid daemon --remote-control run exits successfully without a registered computer or returns immediately after launching its relay worker.

run_control.reason: The operator explicitly requested starting Droid through .dotfiles using the existing Codex-managed-daemon pattern.
